Persistent symptoms after negative initial tests

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A 31-year-old man has ongoing right iliac fossa pain despite initially unremarkable laboratory results and an inconclusive examination. He remains symptomatic at reassessment. Which conclusion is most appropriate when planning his next diagnostic step?

  1. Normal initial tests do not exclude appendicitis; persistent pain warrants further evaluation
  2. A normal leukocyte count guarantees there is no appendicitis
  3. Appendicitis is impossible after one benign examination
  4. Only the first examination should guide care
  5. The patient should never return if pain worsens
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Normal initial tests do not exclude appendicitis; persistent pain warrants further evaluation

Persistent symptoms justify reassessment and appropriate imaging rather than false reassurance.

Understanding the options

Normal initial tests do not exclude appendicitis; persistent pain warrants further evaluation
Persistent symptoms justify reassessment and appropriate imaging rather than false reassurance.
A normal leukocyte count guarantees there is no appendicitis
A single normal result cannot reliably exclude disease.
Appendicitis is impossible after one benign examination
Clinical findings can evolve.
Only the first examination should guide care
Serial assessment can reveal progression.
The patient should never return if pain worsens
Safety-netting and reassessment are important.
